content.title: Kentucky Derby tickets 2026 go on sale this week. Here's what to know and how to buy them
content.text: Nov. 11, 2025, 5:03 a.m. ETTickets are now on sale for the 2026 Kentucky Derby, which will be held on Saturday, May 2, 2026.Seating options range from general admission infield tickets to premium reserved seats with varying prices and views.Tickets can be purchased through the official Kentucky Derby website, Ticketmaster, and various resale sites.The race is on to grab a seat for the 2026 Kentucky Derby.Reserved seating tickets go on sale this week for the world-famous horse race, which will be held on Saturday, May 2, 2026, at the historic Churchill Downs Racetrack.Race fans who missed registering for ticket sales during the pre-sale lottery, which launched in May, now have a chance to purchase purchasing to "The Most Exciting Two Minutes in Sports." If you're someone who doesn't like to gamble on ticket availability, don't let your decision come down to the wire.Most tickets for the Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks, held next year on Friday, May 1, are sold as a two-day package which features all-inclusive food and beverage. Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks two-day ticket packages, which include the infield, go on sale Thursday, Nov. 13.Nearly 150,000 spectators attended the 151st Kentucky Derby this year on May 3, so don't delay.Here is what to know about seating sections and ticket prices for the 2026 Kentucky Oaks and Kentucky Derby.When is the 2026 Kentucky Derby?The 2026 Kentucky Derby will be held Saturday, May 2 at Churchill Downs, 700 Central Ave., in Louisville, Kentucky.How to get Kentucky Derby ticketsThere are plenty of ways to buy Kentucky Derby tickets, but those interested should check for available tickets through the Kentucky Derby website, which will direct you to purchase through kentuckyderby.com, Ticketmaster, Derby Experiences Ticket Package, or by contacting a Kentucky Derby sales representative at sales@kyderby.com.You can also check other resale sites like StubHub and SeatGeek to see at what price tickets are currently selling. Vivid Seats also sells tickets. In some cases, you may be able to save a few bucks when you use a promo code that some ticket sellers make available to first-time users of the platform.How much are tickets to the Kentucky Derby?This varies, widely. General admission tickets for the infield start at $136, while tickets to a Starting Gate Box seat start at $2,241. And you can spend upward of $12,000 for a two-day pass on Millionaires Row.Read more about the various tickets options below.What is the 'all-inclusive' ticket for the 2026 Kentucky Derby?All reserved seats at the Kentucky Derby and Kentucky Oaks include all-inclusive food, nonalcoholic beverages and alcoholic beverages. This change, implemented in 2021, is intended to reduce the amount of time spent in line, eliminating the need for cash transactions for food and beverages and providing the opportunity to try a greater variety of food.What are the ticket, seating options at the Kentucky Derby?We strongly suggest you visit the official Kentucky Derby website before you start your hunt for tickets. The racetrack is a large place with numerous ticket and seating options. You could spend upward of $12,000 for a two-day pass on Millionaires Row or other premium seating options, but more affordable tickets can be found. Some areas will have great views of the racetrack, while in other sections, you'll need to watch the races on a video monitor. Make sure you explore your options before you purchase.Some of the seating options include: Turf Bleachers: Located outdoors on the ground level of the infield and overlooking the dirt and turf racetracks, facing the Grandstand and Homestretch Club. Turf Bleacher guests have access to the Frontside and Paddock areas. Tickets start at $779.Starting Gate Courtyard Reserved Seating: Nestled near the iconic Kentucky Derby starting gate, the Starting Gate Courtyard Reserved Seating offers a variety of new, comfortable padded seating options which may be covered or uncovered. Tickets start at $1,041.Ford First Turn Reserved Seating: Covered seating where you’ll have a view of the horses being paraded from the track to the barn, then out to the paddock right before the race begins. Guests can enjoy expansive views of the whole track from the 2nd and 3rd level. Tickets start at $1,396.Starting Gate Courtyard Rail Boxes: These boxed seats are located near the Kentucky Derby starting gate and offer an a "courtside" experience of the track. Tickets start at $1,604.Clubhouse or Grandstand Box Seating: Boxes have six padded fold-down seats and are located on all three levels (there are covered and uncovered options). Tickets start at $1,765.Homestretch Club: Named for its excellent view of the “home stretch,” this section also has a view of the Big Board and the Winner’s Circle. Seating is uncovered and outdoors, but this clubhouse level also offers access to an air-conditioned club on the first floor with a buffet and private bar. Tickets start at $2,075.Starting Gate Box Seats: Boxes have six padded fold down seats on the third level of the facility. Boxes are located outdoors, overlooking the dirt and turf racetracks, and along the finishing stretch. Tickets start at $2,241.The Final Turn: An upgraded view of the track in the infield where you can bring your own chair or picnic blanket and watch the races from the world’s largest 4K video board. Tickets start at $350.What is the Frontside Plaza Walkaround ticket at the Kentucky Derby?The Frontside Plaza Walkaround ticket offers Plaza and Paddock access with views from the ground along with offsite parking and shuttle access and all-inclusive food and drinks. While you won’t have a seat or direct views of the race, you will experience the races from inside the venue. Tickets start at $695.What are reserved infield bleacher seats at the Kentucky Derby?This is the most affordable “reserved seating” type ticket you can get for the Kentucky Derby.You’ll be able to see the track, and seating includes a view of the final stretch of the Kentucky Derby race and faces the grandstand. It’s uncovered seating so you’re still exposed to the elements, but these seats get you access to the frontside and Paddock areas which includes food and drink, and parking at the Kentucky Exposition Center with a free shuttle to the track. Tickets start at $705.How can I buy general admission infield tickets at the Kentucky Derby?General admission infield tickets are the most budget-friendly on race day and grant you access to the field inside the racetrack. This standing-room-only option is an affordable way to be part of the Kentucky Derby party. Spectators spread out blankets and folding chairs and keep track of their bets while watching the races on the Big Board, a jumbo video screen situated in the center of the track.Infield ticket prices for the Kentucky Oaks and Kentucky Derby start at $139.60 on Nov. 13, then increase to $165 from Nov. 14 through Dec. 25.Reach features reporter Kirby Adams at kadams@courier-journal.com.
